newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - NOV 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - NOV 5.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Today the BBC pledged to become more accountable to the British public in a move similar to John Major's Citizen's Charter Initiative. 250 promises will be made to viewers in a bid to end repeats, curb violence and bad language and cut out 'rottweiler' interviews.
-- D-MARK FEELS PAIN OF YELSTIN HEART-OP

News of Boris Yeltsin's heart bypass operation send traders from trading in the Deutschmark into American, Japanese and Swiss currencies. The dollar was weaker today on fears that the Democrats riding on Clinton's predicted victory could win a clean sweep of Congress and the Senate.
BT MERGER BOOSTS AUSSIE TELECOMS SELL-OFF

According to the Australian Communications Minister Senator Richard Alston the 12.2bn stg BT/MCI merger has strengthened the case for the privatisation of Australian telecoms giant Telstra. He believes that Telstra would be handicapped if it remained 100 percent government owned in today's international telecoms market.

The Petrol Retailers Association wants the Office of Fair Trading to investigate the petrol retail sector. It claims that independent petrol retailers are under threat of being driven out of the market by oil majors rationalising refining capacity who are encouraging supermarkets to ensure supplies.
JF SET TO FACE MORE CLAIMS OVER SCANDAL

Following the fallout from scandal sparked by rogue trader Colin Armstrong, Jardine Fleming is to be hit by claims by two London investors for compensation, for losses incurred investing in the JF Ninja Trust.
